posts.title: Writing Architecture Documents (for developers)
posts.description: Our colleague Martin was about to start working on a small-scale feature, an addition to a module that wasn’t open for extension and couldn’t easily support it. He could shoehorn his use case on top of existing architecture without affecting others much or lay a more robust foundation over which he’d implement his use case. posts.title: I've been writing good, fast, inexpensive software
posts.description: An engineering manager I worked with before asked me how I can deliver good software for lower cost. Am I slow? Is it truly good? Am I losing money? One should always keep such friends close. And it’s a fair question. The old rule in software is good, fast, cheap: pick two. But I provide all three. The short answer is that I changed how I work. The long answer follows.
